lines.text: Place seeds one at a time, turning by the same angle every time. Which angle makes the best sunflower?
A quarter turn gives four straight arms. Lots of wasted space.
A third of a turn gives three arms. Simple fractions always make spokes.
One hundred thirty seven degrees is close, but gaps still appear.
Now the golden angle: about one hundred thirty seven point five degrees.
No gaps. The golden ratio is the hardest number to approximate with fractions, so the seeds never line up.
Count the spirals, and you will find Fibonacci numbers.

post.title: Why 137.5° makes a perfect sunflower
post.description: Seeds placed one by one, each turned by the same angle. Simple fractions make spokes; the golden angle packs every seed. Made with code.
post.pinned_comment: Which angle surprised you most: 90, 120 or 137? What should we grow next?
